exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Only the 10/13 one is valid ($375). The other two trucks were 2-3 hours late for their appointments. I've disputed it with Buckeye; please hold payment until the corrected invoice comes.

exchanges.author: c_omar
exchanges.body: Midstate was late again last week (5 days). we nearly ran out of 16x12x12 boxes. what do you want to do with them?

exchanges.author: c_dale
exchanges.subject: Dock 7 leveler failed
exchanges.body: Ronan, dock 7's hydraulic leveler failed this morning (cylinder leak). Quotes from Rite-Hite: repair $6,800 (new cylinder and seals, 2 days, should get us 2-3 years); full replacement $18,500 (new leveler, 5 days). It's 19 years old. We're down to 11 of 12 doors for peak. Dale

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Approve the $6,800 repair now (within my authority) so we have 12 doors for peak. Please book Rite-Hite for this week. The leveler is 19 years old, so I'll put the $18,500 replacement into a CER for Lisa for the January capital review rather than replacing it in the middle of peak.

exchanges.author: c_shawn
exchanges.subject: Marlene Hughes: final warning?
exchanges.body: Ronan, Marlene Hughes hit 6 points in October (3 full-day absences). She told me she's been taking her mom to dialysis on Tuesdays and Thursdays and her sister usually covers but couldn't. She's a good worker but policy is a final warning at 6. OK to issue it today? Shawn

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Hold the warning, Shawn. Taking a parent to dialysis may be FMLA-protected (caring for a parent with a serious health condition), and she doesn't have to say 'FMLA' for us to be on notice. Under our policy those absences don't count as points until HR decides. Andrea, can you send Marlene the FMLA eligibility notice? We learned about it today, so it's due within five business days. Shawn, please don't discuss it further with her until Andrea reaches out.

exchanges.author: c_lisa
exchanges.subject: Peak staffing plan by Wednesday
exchanges.body: Ronan, please send me the peak labor plan for 11/9-12/18 with Wednesday's pages: hours per day, how we cover them (permanent, OT, agency), and any gap. Forecast attached. Lisa

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Dispute: invoice BF-55102 (detention, October)
exchanges.body: Hello, we dispute part of BF-55102. Detention runs from the appointment time when the truck arrives on time. 10/20 BF-2214 had an 08:00 appointment and arrived 10:40; 10/27 BF-2231 had a 13:00 appointment and arrived 15:50 (gate log attached), so neither qualifies. 10/13 BF-2210 is valid: $375.00. Please reissue for $375.00. Ronan Pierce, Operations Manager, Groveport DC

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Late deliveries and SA-221 rebate
exchanges.body: Joe, four of Midstate's last nine deliveries to Groveport were 4-5 days late (PO-7740, 7802, 7861, 7913), and we nearly ran out of 16x12x12 boxes last week, right before peak. Under SA-221, three late deliveries in a quarter qualify for the 5% rebate on the quarter's purchases; Q3 had two, and Q4 has two already. I need a recovery plan this week: confirmed delivery dates for November, and a safety stock of two weeks of our top 5 sizes on your floor. Ronan

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# Groveport peak labor plan, 11/9-12/18 (draft for Lisa)

Demand: 13,200 lines a day average (peak day ~15,400).
Productivity: 7.65 lines per labor hour (October: 253,460 lines / 33,120 hours).
Hours needed: 13,200 / 7.65 = 1,725 a day.
Coverage: permanent 148 associates x 8 h x 95% attendance = 1,125; overtime capped at 10% of straight time = 112; agency 488 hours a day = 61 agency FTE.
Agency on hand: ~30 FTE (5,260 hours in October / 22 days / 8) + peak class of 24 on 11/9 = 54. Gap: ~7 FTE (56 hours a day).
Options: a second Pinnacle class of 8 by 11/16 (preferred: 56 h x $29.00 = $1,624 a day), or 56 more overtime hours a day (OT ~15% of straight time; 56 h x $30.90 = $1,730 a day, plus fatigue risk in peak), or both on peak days. Either is beyond the approved plan, so it needs your approval.
Peak days (~15,400 lines, 2,013 hours) need the second class plus Saturday shifts.
